results.title: Rs 200 ginger, Rs 80 tomatoes! Odisha flood impact hits kitchen budget
results.description: Household budgets in Odisha have come under pressure due to the recent floods across various regions in the state. The prices of several vegetables and essential grocery items increased sharply in recent days. As per reports, sugar recorded a notable rise after its retail price increased from around Rs 55 per kg two weeks ago to Rs 65 per kg. Traders reportedly said that the increase in sugar prices was partly linked to the diversion of sugarcane for ethanol production. Supply disruptions also reportedly contributed to higher vegetable prices. Rise In Vegetable Prices Onion prices have climbed from around Rs 40 to Rs 50 per kg. Tomatoes are now being sold at around Rs 80 per kg, while cabbage is priced at Rs 30, carrot at Rs 50, pointed gourd (potala) at Rs 50, bitter gourd at Rs 50-60 and brinjal at Rs 50-60. Ridge gourd is being sold for around Rs 80 per kg, while the prices of spine gourd and ginger touched Rs 200. Garlic is available at around Rs 240 per kg. Papaya prices went up from Rs 20 to Rs 25, while potato rose from Rs 20 to Rs 22. Beans sourced from outside Odisha are priced at around Rs 160 per kg, while Koraput beans cost Rs 80-100. Oil, Cumin Prices Also Up Refined edible oil is priced at around Rs 180 per litre. Mustard oil is available at Rs 200-220 per litre. Traders said that the prices of both oil and sugar increased by around Rs 10 per litre within a week. Cumin prices also rose by nearly Rs 20 to around Rs 290 per kg. Rainfall in Nashik reportedly disrupted onion supplies which contributed to the price rise in Odisha. Onion prices are expected to increase further in the coming days. Also Read: Odisha floods: Subarnarekha river breaches danger level in Balasore; 48 panchayats affected The rising cost of basic food items have indirectly added to the financial burden on consumers which have forced households to spend more on everyday cooking essentials.
